extraction.notes: Long source (134 pages). Read the contents pages (2-3) and in full: Part 1 problem analysis, objectives, consistency and key priorities (pages 9-25), mainstreaming (page 26), public procurement (page 28), public administration reform (pages 32-35), cybersecurity and digitalisation sub-areas 2.2.1 and 2.2.2 (pages 50-58), education reforms 3.1.3 to 3.1.5 (pages 63-68), business environment passages on digital services, SME charges, innovation hubs, E-Customs, ITS and e-freight (pages 69, 72, 77, 79-80, 82, 85, 87-95), and complementarity and WBIF (pages 117, 120-122, 124, 134). A keyword screen ran over the whole text (digital, cyber, artificial intelligence, AI, interoperab, electronic, e- prefixed services, personal data, data protection, broadband, 5G, online, portal, ICT, IT, information system, platform, database, foreign, foreigner, EURES, social security, social insurance, migrant, free movement, work permit, health insurance, Labour Authority, equal treatment, emigration, mobility); pages not listed above were screened only. Annex 1 of the Agenda is registered separately as MKD-GOV-2024-002. No Chapter 2 content: the screen found no claim on EU or foreign workers' rights or access, EURES, the European Labour Authority, social security coordination or the European Health Insurance Card. Left out as general labour-market policy or emigration: labour market analysis (pages 14-15), informal work, seasonal work law and the wage guarantee mechanism (pages 69-74), and references to brain drain and emigration; 'mobility of skilled workforce' on page 95 is a general regional integration aim. Left out as back-office or sector systems under the materiality test: IFMIS, ITIS, the Public Revenue Office system and its upgrade for seasonal work (pages 14, 72), the state aid management information system (page 14), the transitory public investment IT solution (page 32), HRMIS staffing data (page 35), the court case management system and ICT Council (pages 17, 104-106), prosecution and asset recovery databases (pages 109-114), ITS road deployment and rail standards other than the European Vehicle Register (pages 90-95), and internal monitoring data systems (pages 123-124). Left out as incidental: general statements on the benefits of digitalisation (page 13), digital tools and corruption (page 13), the Open Finance website (page 10), digital transformation and gender equality (page 25), the IPA III comparison table (page 117), digital innovation mentioned only as a Smart Specialisation domain (page 80), renewable energy registries and trading platforms (pages 43-44), and smart grids (page 120). Cybercrime references (pages 53, 110, 117) were left out as cybercrime law enforcement. Left out as digital skills not directly linked to an in-scope recommendation: VET and curricula digital competences (pages 15, 20, 23, 59, 62-63, 65-66), including the teacher training and curricula steps under reform 3.1.4. Baselines stated only as 'Baseline (2024) is 0' were not extracted as metrics; they add no measured value. Activity lists under each step were extracted only where they state something the step does not. Steps and targets are interventions with proposed status, and their stated dates are recorded as event dates. Claims repeated in the running text are extracted at each place, as the rules require, and pass 2 should link them. Page 5 of the abbreviations list defines eIDAS as 'Enhanced Data Protection Measures', which does not match how the term is used in the body; it was not extracted. The Agenda was drafted in 2024 and speaks of the situation at that time; the text was not checked against later events. Many passages cite the Commission's 2023 report through the Government's own text; these are flagged reported_view. Spaces inside words are as printed in the converted text. Second-pass check done (G3 condition 2). Items 0144 to 0149 are splits and 0150 to 0169 were added by the second-pass checker; see review/RUN-2026-01/second_pass/.
